title: Analytic structure-sheaf vanishing on projective space
statement: Let $n\geq0$, and let $P^{\mathrm{an}}=\mathbf P^n(\mathbf C)$ be complex projective space, with its standard holomorphic charts and sheaf $\mathcal O_{P^{\mathrm{an}}}$ of holomorphic functions. Every global holomorphic function on $P^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a unique constant. For every integer $q>0$ the analytic sheaf cohomology group $H^q(P^{\mathrm{an}},\mathcal O_{P^{\mathrm{an}}})$ is zero, where cohomology is right derived global sections in sheaves of $\mathbf C$-vector spaces. This includes $n=0$, the one-point analytic space. Use module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] with the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf C$.

source.place: WANTED: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §13 Lemma 4 and its Dolbeault proof, printed pp.20--21.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^n(\mathbf C)$. Apply [lem-sfb-analytic-projective-kahler-geometry] to equip this very analytic space, with the charts of the statement, with its compact Kähler metric; in particular it is Hausdorff and second-countable. Use the site of its open subsets, in a universe containing that set, with terminal object $P$, and the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf C$. The module category has enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. By [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] with $p=0$, $\mathcal O_P[0]\to\mathcal A_P^{0,\bullet}$ is an exact augmented resolution with global-section-acyclic terms. Apply the acyclic-resolution comparisons in [lem-sfb-ringed-acyclic-resolution-derived-maps] with identity ringed-topos morphism, both modules equal to $\mathcal O_P$, both resolutions this one and $u=\mathrm{id}$. Taking cohomology identifies the underlying groups of $H^q(P,\mathcal O_P)$ with $\ker(\bar\partial:A^{0,q}\to A^{0,q+1})/\bar\partial A^{0,q-1}$. Thus vanishing of this Dolbeault quotient implies the requested vanishing in complex-vector-space sheaves; no change to algebraic cohomology is being made.

proof.text:
Suppose $n\geq1$. For a holomorphic function $f$ on $P$, the function $u=f\circ\pi$ is holomorphic on $\mathbf C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$: in $z_j
e0$ it is $f$ in chart coordinates composed with $(z_k/z_j)_{k
e j}$, using [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]. By [lem-sfb-hartogs-punctured-affine-extension] it extends to an entire $F$. Scalar multiplication does not change $\pi$, so for $z
e0$ and real $t>0$ one has $F(tz)=F(z)$. Continuity of $F$ at $0$, supplied by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations], gives $F(z)=F(0)$ as $t	o0$. Surjectivity of $\pi$ gives $f=F(0)$. Conversely every constant is holomorphic by the same operations node, and evaluating at $[1:0:\cdots:0]$ proves uniqueness.

proof.text: Still let $n\geq1$ and $1\leq r\leq n$. For a global holomorphic $r$-form $\beta$ on $P$, write $\pi^*\beta=\sum_{|I|=r}b_I(z)\,dz_I$ on $\mathbf C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$. Each $b_I$ is holomorphic: on $z_j\ne0$ substitute the chart functions $z_k/z_j$ into the coefficients of $\beta$ and expand $d(z_k/z_j)=(z_jdz_k-z_kdz_j)/z_j^2$, using [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations] and [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-derivative-rules]. Hartogs extension [lem-sfb-hartogs-punctured-affine-extension] gives entire coefficients $B_I$. Since $\pi(tz)=\pi(z)$, substituting $tz$ and $d(tz)=t\,dz$ gives $t^r B_I(tz)=B_I(z)$ for $z\ne0$, $t>0$. Continuity at the origin and $r>0$ force $B_I(z)=0$ by letting $t\to0$. Hence $\pi^*\beta=0$, and pulling this back by each explicitly given local section $s_j$ in [lem-sfb-analytic-projective-kahler-geometry] gives $\beta|_{U_j}=0$. These opens cover $P$, so $\beta=0$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §13 Lemma 4, printed pp.20--21; read online https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf. Agent expansion of the Dolbeault/Kähler argument.

proof.text: For $1\leq q\leq n$, choose a Dolbeault cocycle $a\in A^{0,q}(P)$. The orthogonal decomposition [lem-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-orthogonal-decomposition], applicable to the compact Hermitian manifold from step 1, writes $a=h+\bar\partial u+\bar\partial^*v$ with $\Delta_{\bar\partial}h=0$. By the defining formal-adjoint identity, $0=\langle\Delta_{\bar\partial}h,h\rangle=\|\bar\partial h\|^2+\|\bar\partial^*h\|^2$, so $\bar\partial h=0$. As $\bar\partial^2=0$ by [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] and $\bar\partial a=0$, the residual term $w=\bar\partial^*v$ is closed. Then $\|w\|^2=\langle\bar\partial w,v\rangle=0$, so $a$ and $h$ represent the same class. Here norms are the $L^2$ norms on smooth forms; zero norm implies the form is zero since a smooth nonzero form is nonzero on an open set of positive metric volume.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §13 Lemma 4, printed pp.20--21; read online https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf. Agent expansion of the Dolbeault/Kähler argument.

proof.text: The Kähler hypothesis from step 1 allows [lem-sfb-kahler-laplacian-identity] to give $\Delta_d h=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}h=0$. Its formal adjoints therefore give $0=\langle\Delta_dh,h\rangle=\|dh\|^2+\|d^*h\|^2$, whence $dh=0$. Coefficientwise complex conjugation commutes with $d$ (differentiate real coordinates), so $\beta=\overline h$ is a closed smooth form of type $(q,0)$. The distinct-type components of $d\beta=\partial\beta+\bar\partial\beta=0$ imply $\bar\partial\beta=0$. Exactness at $\mathcal A^{q,0}$ in [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] says precisely that $\beta$ is a holomorphic $q$-form. Step 3 gives $\beta=0$, hence $h=0$ and the class of $a$ is zero. Step 1 now gives $H^q(P,\mathcal O_P)=0$.

proof.text: For $q>n$, $A^{0,q}(P)=0$ by its definition as alternating forms in $n$ antiholomorphic coordinate differentials, so the quotient in step 1 vanishes. If $n=0$, $P$ is a single point, with $\mathcal O_P(P)=\mathbf C$, and all positive-degree smooth forms vanish for the same reason. Thus the same comparison in step 1 proves every positive-degree vanishing also in this case; evaluation at that point identifies its holomorphic functions with unique constants.
